newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases offshore, interbank rate up late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases offshore, interbank rate up late.

text.p: The Thai baht eased against the dollar in late Monday trade on easing demand for baht and falling swap premiums, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 24.900/25.100 to the dollar late in offshore market compared with 24.500/24.700 in early moring.
"The (baht/dollar) spot rate fell in line with the easing swap premiums. The baht demand is easing today," said one Singapore-based dealer.
Offshore parties had chased baht in past weeks to cover their short posititions made during the speculative attack on the baht in mid-May.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium decreased to 155/185 satangs per dollar late in offshore market from 240/270 in the morning.

In the domestic market, baht trading remained cautious with continued buying of the dollar on concerns about the government's economic policies after the appointment of new finance minister Thanong Bidaya, dealers said.
The baht was traded at 25.950/26.050 late in the local market against 26.000/26.100 in the morning. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.81.
Low-profile banker Thanong was appointed on Friday after Amnuay quit abruptly on Thursday following differences with his political rivals in the coalition government of premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

Thanong pledged at a news conference on Friday that he would pursue Amnuay's fiscal and monetary policies, saying they were mostly on the right track in tackling Thailand's worst economic slump in over a decade.
The one-month swap premium was quoted at 20.30 satangs late compared with 20/35 in the morning in the domestic market.
The overnight interbank rate rose to 18.00-20.00 percent from 18.00 percent in the morning as heavy buying of the dollar squeezed domestic banking liquidity, dealers said.
